Lumentum: U.S. maker of lasers and optical components for data centers and telecom networks, including the laser chips inside high-speed transceivers.
Coherent: U.S. company that makes optical transceivers, lasers and engineered materials for data centers, telecom and industrial customers.
Ciena: U.S. supplier of optical networking systems and software that carriers and cloud companies use to move data over fiber between sites.
Fabrinet: Contract manufacturer, with its main plants in Thailand, that assembles precision optical products for other photonics companies.
IPG Photonics: Maker of high-power fiber lasers used for cutting, welding and other industrial work.
nLIGHT: U.S. maker of semiconductor and fiber lasers for industrial, aerospace and defense uses, including directed energy.
Zhongji Innolight: China-listed maker of high-speed optical transceiver modules and one of the largest suppliers to cloud data centers.
Eoptolink: China-listed maker of optical transceiver modules for data centers and telecom networks.
Suzhou TFC Optical: China-listed maker of optical components and packaging used inside transceivers.
Applied Optoelectronics: U.S. maker of lasers and optical transceivers for data centers and cable broadband networks.
Aixtron: German maker of deposition equipment used to grow the compound semiconductor layers inside lasers and other optical chips.
AXT Inc: Maker of indium phosphide and other compound semiconductor wafers that laser and photodetector chips are built on.
LandMark Optoelectronics: Taiwan-listed maker of epitaxial wafers for lasers and photodetectors used in optical communications.
Semtech: U.S. chip company whose products include the signal integrity chips used in optical modules and active cables.
Win Semiconductors: Taiwan-listed compound semiconductor foundry that manufactures optical and radio chips for other companies.
Tower Semiconductor: Israeli specialty chip foundry with a silicon photonics manufacturing platform used by optical chip designers.
Yuanjie Semiconductor: China-listed maker of laser chips for optical communications.
MACOM Technology: U.S. maker of analog and optical semiconductor components for data centers, telecom and defense.
Soitec: French maker of engineered wafers, including silicon-on-insulator wafers used for silicon photonics.
Nokia: Finnish network equipment company with a large optical networking business, expanded through its purchase of Infinera.
Credo Technology: Maker of high-speed connectivity chips and active electrical cables used to link servers and switches in AI data centers.
Broadcom: Large U.S. chip company whose products include data center switch chips, optical components and co-packaged optics.
Arista Networks: U.S. maker of data center network switches, which are among the biggest users of optical transceivers.
Amphenol: Large U.S. maker of connectors, cables and fiber optic interconnect products.
TSMC: The world's largest contract chip manufacturer and the biggest buyer of EUV lithography machines. It also packages silicon photonics chips.
ASML: Dutch company that is the only maker of the extreme ultraviolet lithography machines used to print the most advanced chips.
Applied Materials: Largest U.S. maker of chip manufacturing equipment.
Lam Research: U.S. maker of etch and deposition equipment for chip manufacturing.
KLA: U.S. maker of inspection and measurement tools that use optics to find defects on chips.
Corning: U.S. glass and materials company and one of the largest makers of optical fiber and cable.
Entegris: U.S. supplier of specialty chemicals, filters and materials used in chip manufacturing.
Astera Labs: U.S. maker of connectivity chips for AI servers.
Seagate: Maker of hard disk drives used for mass data storage.
eMemory: Taiwan-listed company that licenses embedded memory designs to chipmakers.
Western Digital: Maker of hard disk drives for data centers.
Micron: U.S. maker of memory chips, including the high-bandwidth memory used with AI processors.
Marvell: U.S. chip company whose products include the signal processing chips inside optical transceivers and custom AI chips.
Anthropic (private, via SPV): Privately held AI company. It is not a photonics company; the fund holds it as a private position through a special purpose vehicle.
Ayar Labs (private): Privately held U.S. startup that develops optical chip-to-chip links meant to replace copper connections inside AI systems.
